- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment spikes) — model tends to overshoot after sentiment turns positive.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment periods (negative sentiment) — model consistently underreacts to negative sentiment, especially when sentiment is strong and sustained.
- Lag in downward corrections — model delays price declines, often forecasting a dip too late or too slowly when sentiment turns negative.
- Mean reversion bias — model overcorrects after sharp spikes, leading to overprediction of subsequent declines.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early cycles (e.g., 2025-02-18) when sentiment is mixed or mildly negative — model fails to account for sentiment decay.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trends — model often assumes momentum continues when sentiment reverses or weakens, especially after 3–5 days of negative sentiment.
- Adjust for sentiment volatility — when sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from -0.5 to +0.3), model fails to adjust forecast mid-cycle, leading to misalignment with true price behavior.
